study.title: Brain sensory network activity underlies reduced nociceptive initiated and nociplastic pain via acupuncture in fibromyalgia
study.study_design: single-site, blinded, sham-controlled, randomized, non-crossover longitudinal neuroimaging trial; secondary analysis of data from the trial
study.blinding: blinded; both groups wore blindfolds during treatment and received identical verbal instructions and treatment durations
study.population: Female adults with fibromyalgia, all female and right-handed
study.inclusion_criteria: Diagnosed with FM, met the 2011 FM Survey Criteria, self-reported symptoms for at least one year, pain on more than 50% of days, and a pain score of >= 4 on a 10 cm Visual Analog Scale (VAS); female and right-handed
study.exclusion_criteria: Having received acupuncture within the last 6 months, neurological disorders such as peripheral neuropathy, psychiatric conditions (e.g., schizophrenia, major depression with suicidal ideation), substance abuse, use of opioids or stimulant medications, and contraindications to MRI or electrostimulation

arms.dropouts: Of 70 participants with clinical data, 26 were excluded due to missing either baseline or post-treatment evoked pain scans; final fMRI sample EA: 19

extraction_notes.note: Adverse events are not reported anywhere in the manuscript. No statement is made about whether adverse events occurred or were monitored.
Deqi sensation was not measured or reported in this study. The paper does not discuss whether deqi was elicited during electroacupuncture sessions.

Sample sizes differ between clinical (EA n=33, ML n=37, total n=70) and neuroimaging (EA n=19, ML n=25, total n=44) analyses. The clinical sample sizes for PPTol/widespread pain correlations (n=33 EA, n=37 ML) are larger than the fMRI subsample, suggesting these behavioral data come from a broader sample than the neuroimaging subsample. This is noted in Figure 2 legend.

Supplemental Tables 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 are referenced but not provided. Table 1 contains clinical characteristics and participant demographics for full sample and fMRI subsample. Table 3 contains block design timing parameters. Table 4 contains detailed information on significant gPPI clusters (coordinates not available from main text). Table 5 contains additional mediation results including ML precuneus-aIC mediation and EA S1-aIC supplemental mediation.
Supplemental Figure 1 shows an example mediation model but was not provided. Cannot extract visual details.

The gPPI analysis clusters are described in text but their MNI coordinates are stated to be in Supplemental Table 4, which was not provided. Only seed coordinates are available from Table 1 in the main text. The resulting cluster coordinates (e.g., L S1 cluster for R aIC seed, L precuneus cluster for R aIC seed in ML) are not reported in the main text with numeric coordinates.

Spearman rho values for activation-widespread pain correlations per group (e.g., EA rho=-0.78 for L S1, rho=-0.67 for R S1, rho=-0.72 for L Cingulate, rho=-0.85 for L Precuneus; ML rho=0.27, 0.37, 0.32, 0.56 respectively) were extracted from Figure 3b scatter plot labels and figure caption descriptions, not from a results table. These may be less precise than table-reported values.

The serial mediation path coefficient X→M1 in the EA model is reported as β=-0.40 in Figure 5 but the corresponding X→M (pain tolerance to L S1 activation) in Table 3 is Beta=0.41. The sign difference may reflect different directions of variable coding (change in widespread pain vs. reduction) in Figure 5 diagram vs. Table 3. This inconsistency is noted.

Specific electrical stimulation parameters (pulse width, exact frequency values, intensity values in mA) for electroacupuncture are stated to be individualized to participants' sensory and pain thresholds and described as 'low-frequency'; full details stated to be in prior publication (Mawla et al. 2021).
Number of participants assigned to each arm at randomization is not reported in this paper. The paper only reports final analyzed sample sizes.

This paper explicitly states it presents a secondary analysis of data from the trial (NCT02064296). The primary endpoint (Brief Pain Inventory pain severity) and key secondary endpoints have been published previously (Mawla et al. 2021, Arthritis Rheumatol). Results reported here are new analyses not previously published.

The indirect effect CI for the EA serial mediation is reported as [-6.00, -0.00] which spans a wide range. This appears as reported in Figure 5. This may reflect small sample size or bootstrapping artifact and is extracted as reported.

Pain assessments were conducted a few days prior to the MRI sessions due to logistical constraints, introducing potential temporal separation between behavioral and imaging measures. Authors note this as a limitation.
Expectancy (as distinct from credibility) was not formally assessed. The paper discusses credibility via the Credibility Questionnaire but does not report expectancy measures separately.
The study excluded males; all participants were female and right-handed. Authors note findings may not generalize to males.

The coordinate reported for Left somatosensory cortex (L S1) in Table 1 (ROI for gPPI) is -8, -38, 68 - which is the same as the peak coordinate for the L S1 activation cluster in Table 2. This suggests the gPPI seed was defined from the activation cluster. The R S1 coordinates in Table 1 are 20, -34, 66, also matching Table 2.
